title: Understanding Regularization
text: Regularization is a technique used to prevent overfitting in models by adding a penalty term to the loss function. The two most common types are L1 (Lasso) and L2 (Ridge) regularization.

title: L1 vs L2 Regularization
text: L1 regularization adds the absolute value of the coefficients as a penalty term, while L2 regularization adds the square of the coefficients.

title: Effect of Lambda on Regularization
text: The lambda (λ) hyperparameter controls the strength of the penalty term in regularization. A higher λ increases the penalty, leading to simpler models.

title: Optimal Lambda for L1 and L2
text: The optimal λ for L1 and L2 regularization may differ because they penalize the coefficients differently. L1 tends to produce sparse models, while L2 tends to shrink coefficients evenly.
